title: Lok Sabha election of 1984
body: In the Lok Sabha elections of 1984, the Congress party won 415 of the 543 Lok Sabha seats, a victory never achieved before by any party. Some results of that election were: Congress 48.0% of votes and 415 seats; BJP 7.4% of votes and 2 seats; Janata 6.7% and 10 seats; Lok Dal 5.7% and 3 seats; CPI (M) 5.7% and 22 seats; Telugu Desam 4.1% and 30 seats; AIADMK 1.6% and 12 seats. India follows a method in which the country is divided into constituencies, each constituency elects one representative, and the candidate who secures the highest number of votes in that constituency is declared elected.

title: The Election Commission in difficult situations
body: Since 1951-52 the Election Commission of India has conducted many Lok Sabha, State Assembly and by-elections. It has held elections in militancy-affected areas such as Assam, Punjab and Jammu and Kashmir. In 1991 it had to postpone the election process mid-way when the former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated during campaigning. In 2002 the Gujarat Assembly was dissolved and elections were due, but the Commission found that unprecedented violence in the State made it impossible to hold free and fair elections immediately. It postponed the Assembly elections by a few months, and the Supreme Court upheld this decision.
